incident.message: FailedMount: MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "settings" : configmap "app-settings" not found

classification.rationale: The pod failed to mount a volume because the referenced ConfigMap "app-settings" does not exist, indicating a storage or configuration resource availability issue.

diagnosis.root_cause: The Deployment's pod spec mounts a volume named 'settings' sourced from ConfigMap 'app-settings', but that ConfigMap does not exist in namespace 'lab-14'. Kubernetes cannot set up the volume, so the container is permanently stuck in ContainerCreating and will never start until the ConfigMap is created.

evidence.value: MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "settings" : configmap "app-settings" not found

proposal.rationale: The ConfigMap 'app-settings' referenced by the 'settings' volume in Deployment 'viewer-7050e9' (namespace 'lab-14') does not exist. This is not a PVC/StorageClass issue — it is a missing ConfigMap. The fix is outside the scope of storage field changes: a human (or GitOps pipeline) must create the 'app-settings' ConfigMap in namespace 'lab-14' with the correct keys and values expected by the application. Check: (1) Git history / Helm chart values for the expected contents of 'app-settings'; (2) Whether the ConfigMap exists in other environments/namespaces as a reference; (3) Whether the Deployment's volumeMount spec references the right name.
proposal.risk: No automated fix available. The pod will remain stuck indefinitely until the ConfigMap is created with the correct content.
proposal.delivery: Apply as a pull request against /gitops after a human approves it. The agent does not change the cluster.

similar_incidents.title: PM-2026-085: analytics-cache stuck Pending on a StorageClass that did not exist
similar_incidents.fix: Changed spec.storageClassName of the PVC to a StorageClass that exists in the cluster and recreated the claim (the field is immutable; the claim had never bound, so no data was lost). The pod's FailedScheduling had the same cause.
similar_incidents.excerpt: This cluster's StorageClasses were `gp2` (in-tree) and `gp3` (EBS CSI); there was no `fast-ssd` and no default class. `storageClassName` cannot be changed on an existing claim, so the claim had to be recreated with the right class. ## Evidence - PVC events: `ProvisioningFailed: storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found`. - PVC `status.phase: Pending`, no `volumeName`. - Pod events: `0/3 nod

similar_incidents.title: PM-2026-091: node disk pressure evicted pods after container logs filled the root volume
similar_incidents.fix: Turned off the debug logging, set resources.limits.ephemeral-storage 2Gi and an emptyDir sizeLimit of 1Gi on the noisy container, and replaced the affected node. Clue: evictions of unrelated pods on one node with DiskPressure=True.
